newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LOVE'S VICTORY A FAMILY AFFAIR AT PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LOVE'S VICTORY A FAMILY AFFAIR AT PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Davis Love's victory in the PGA Championship on Sunday was a real family affair.
The 33-year-old Love won his first major championship with his brother at his side, his mother, sister and wife in the gallery and his late father in all of their thoughts.

Love, a winner of 10 other tournaments in a distinguished career, refused to single out any one of the them in particular but gave credit to all of them for helping him reach a pinnacle in life that was always his goal.

It would have been easy, and perhaps understandable, for Love to give all the credit for his victory to his father and namesake, a famous teaching professional who taught him the game and gave him guiding principles by which to live.
"I think about my dad a lot," Love said, keeeping things in perspective. "I thought about him last week missing the cut and I thought about him winning this week."
Love, however, declined to "dedicate" his victory to his father, Davis Love Jr, who died in a plane crash in 1988.
"I always said I would never do that because every day I play golf I think about my dad," Love said.

But he added: "To be the son of a PGA professional and to win the PGA Championship is quite a thrill. He played here in '74 (in the U.S. Open), he played in four or five PGAs and a lot of Opens. He was thrilled to be a part of it and so am I."
Love's brother, Mark, was also a big part of his victory. He has been the new champion's caddie for many years and walked every step to victory with his brother.
"He has given me an awful lot to help me achieve my goals," Love said. "He wanted to be a (golf) teacher and I talked him into being a teacher for just one person -- to help me with my golf game.
"He's carrying a golf bag in the pouring rain and in the dark...to help me with my career. I know I could not have done it without him.
"My dad would have been proud of what he's done."
Love also praised his wife, Robin, for "letting her husband do what he does, travel the world playing golf. She's very special, too."
Love saved some of his most lavish praise for his mother, Penta.
"She's been a great inspiration to me the way she's handled her life since my dad passed away.
"If I had to dedicate my victory to anyone, it would probably be my mom for putting up with me for the last eight or nine years and supporting me so much."
But her support did not start recently.
"My mom drove me to tournaments when I was a kid. She's the only one who could take me out to play at Atlanta Country Club because my dad was working and I had to play with an adult.
"She supported my career as much or more than my dad did.
"She a wonderful golfer and I'm sure that I get at least half my golfing abilities from her."
But Love did not really want to single out anyone for special praise.

"I couldn't have done it without a whole lot of support from a whole lot of people," Love said, barely controlling his emotions. "My wife and my friends and my family, we had a lot of fun doing it this week."
Still, in the moment of his greatest triumph, Davis Love III had the highest compliment for Davis Love Jr.
"Golf would not be golf without my father or his memory," the winner of the 79th PGA Championship said.
